name: hippocratic-bedside-diagnosis
description: Greek physicians taught doctors to read a patient's skin, pulse and breathing to judge the course of an illness.

name: herophilus-pulse-timing
description: An Alexandrian physician measured the pulse against a water clock and linked its rhythm to health and disease.

name: wang-shuhe-pulse-classic
description: A Chinese physician compiled a classic text sorting the pulse into many types, each read as a sign of illness.

name: santorio-body-thermometer
description: An Italian physician placed a thermoscope in a patient's mouth, an early attempt to put a number on body heat.

name: leeuwenhoek-blood-cells
description: A Dutch cloth merchant using homemade lenses was the first to describe red blood cells under a microscope.

name: auenbrugger-chest-percussion
description: A Viennese doctor published a method of tapping the chest and listening to the sound to detect fluid and disease.

name: bozzini-light-conductor
description: A German physician reflected candlelight down a tube to peer into body cavities, the forerunner of the endoscope.

name: riva-rocci-blood-pressure-cuff
description: An Italian doctor wrapped an inflatable cuff around the upper arm, giving a simple, reliable way to read blood pressure.

name: berger-eeg-recorded
description: A German psychiatrist attached electrodes to a human scalp and recorded the brain's electrical rhythms for the first time.

name: papanicolaou-smear-test
description: A Greek-American scientist showed that cells taken from the cervix could reveal cancer before symptoms appeared.

name: forssmann-heart-catheter
description: A young German doctor pushed a tube through a vein in his own arm into his heart, then walked to get an X-ray.

name: apgar-score-newborns
description: An American anaesthesiologist devised a quick five-point check of a baby's health in the first minutes after birth.

name: hirschowitz-fibre-optic-endoscope
description: A flexible bundle of glass fibres carried light so doctors could view the inside of a living patient's stomach.

name: first-ct-scan-patient
friendly_name: First CT Scan of a Patient
description: A London hospital used a rotating X-ray machine and a computer to image a woman's brain slice by slice.

name: home-pregnancy-test-launched
description: A boxed kit with a test tube and chemicals let women check for pregnancy in private rather than at a doctor's office.

name: first-mri-human-scan
friendly_name: First MRI Scan of a Human
description: A huge magnet and radio waves produced an image of a man's chest without any radiation.

name: first-hiv-blood-test
description: Blood banks began screening donations with an antibody test for the virus that causes AIDS.

name: fmri-brain-imaging
description: Researchers used magnetic scanning to show blood flow changes in a living human brain as it responded to tasks.

name: capsule-endoscopy-camera-pill
description: A pill-sized camera that patients swallow was reported to film the whole digestive tract as it passed through.

name: smartwatch-ecg-approved
description: A wrist-worn consumer watch gained approval to record a heart tracing and flag an irregular rhythm.

name: mass-covid-testing
friendly_name: Mass Testing for a New Virus
description: Swab tests and rapid kits were used by millions to check for infection with a newly emerged virus.
